provenanceNote: Curated from two secondary references — the AHA 2022 Scientific Statement (Table 3) and Hellfritzsch et al. 2024 (100 agents evaluated) — plus FDA DOAC labeling, and applied consistently across the original 52 agents; the ibrutinib entry was re-sourced in v1.1.0 to its FDA labeling and the 2025 ACC cardio-oncology guidance. v1.2.0 (OpenEvidence review 4) corrected 16 RxNorm codes, re-rated 8 agents and added 18 agents (70 total); new reference-only cells not yet reviewed are rated unknown. The per-agent `sources` array is a KB-level attestation, not per-interaction citation. All `major` cells are individually anchored via `evidenceAnchor`: the 22 recommendation-changing cells (11 agents × apixaban/rivaroxaban) plus 4 reference-only dabigatran/edoxaban cells. Each major cell states its `exposure` direction (increased = bleeding risk; decreased = loss of efficacy). Several majors rest on expert guidance rather than FDA label text (idelalisib, enzalutamide, mitotane, tucatinib), and say so. Quantitative magnitudes in `mechanism` strings are as reported in these secondary references, not independently re-derived. `lastReviewed` is the author curation date and does NOT denote clinician validation (F13). Not for clinical use without pharmacist/clinician sign-off.

apixaban.mechanism: Ibrutinib impairs platelet function via BTK/Tec inhibition, adding to the anticoagulant's bleeding risk; any CYP3A4/P-gp-mediated rise in apixaban level is modest and not clinically significant.
apixaban.recommendation: Factor Xa inhibitors are the preferred anticoagulant with ibrutinib. Co-prescribe if benefit outweighs bleeding risk and monitor for bleeding.

evidenceAnchor.source: Ganatra S, Barac A, Armenian S, et al. 2025 ACC Concise Clinical Guidance (BTK, immune checkpoint, VEGF inhibitors). J Am Coll Cardiol, online Feb 10 2026; FDA Imbruvica (ibrutinib) prescribing information, 2025
evidenceAnchor.locator: ACC section 4.1.5, Table 4, Figure 2 (dabigatran should not be coadministered; no significant adverse events observed with factor Xa inhibitors); Imbruvica §5.1 Hemorrhage, §7 Drug Interactions, §12.3 Clinical Pharmacology
evidenceAnchor.claim: Interaction is pharmacodynamic (platelet inhibition); factor Xa inhibitors preferred with ibrutinib

rivaroxaban.mechanism: Same platelet-mediated additive bleeding mechanism; no validated clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction.
rivaroxaban.recommendation: Acceptable with bleeding monitoring; one retrospective series reported more major bleeding with rivaroxaban than apixaban, so apixaban may be preferable.

dabigatran.mechanism: Ibrutinib's P-gp inhibition can raise levels of dabigatran (the most P-gp-dependent DOAC), compounding ibrutinib's intrinsic platelet/bleeding effect.
dabigatran.recommendation: AVOID. Use a factor Xa inhibitor instead.

edoxaban.mechanism: Predominantly additive bleeding from platelet inhibition; edoxaban is a P-gp substrate, so a modest level increase is possible.
edoxaban.recommendation: Acceptable; factor Xa inhibitors, including edoxaban, are preferred with ibrutinib. Monitor for bleeding.
